newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit softer on offshore selling, dlr strength.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit softer on offshore selling, dlr strength.

text.p: The ringgit fell against the dollar in early Asian trading, pressured by dollar buying by offshore players and strength in the dollar/majors, dealers said.
But corporate selling interest out of Kuala Lumpur would again cap the dollar's rise at 2.5180/90, they said.
"There are selling orders from local corporates at 2.5180 level. It will be tough for dollar/ringgit to get close to 2.5200," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
Dealers said lack of fresh leads would keep the ringgit rangebound through the day.
At 0230 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5165/70 a dollar against its opening around 2.5155/60 and 2.5150/60 at close in Kuala Lumpur on Friday.
For the near term, dealers were expecting the dollar/ringgit to continue trading in the 2.5050-2.5200 range.
